The async semaphore binds to the event loop on first use (asyncio.Semaphore in Python>=3.10 binds lazily on first contended wait; using it across loops, e.g. repeated asyncio.run in tests, may raise - INFERRED). Multiple uvicorn workers / separate processes each get their own cap. Call sites: clients.py L113 (sync), orchestrator.py L249 (sync, backend=='cborg'), kg_rag_api.py L1455 (async). Not used by extract_terms.py, nor around Orchestrator tool-internal llm_invoke (covered by outer slot only). kg_rag_api's direct-script fallback import (L74 'from cborg_limiter import async_slot') would load a second module instance with its own semaphore.

items.notes: Evaluated on every client construction. Because f2w_agent sub-agents and api._chat_completion build a new client per LLM call, IPv6 mode runs a UDP probe and possibly an `ifconfig` subprocess per call and creates an httpx client that is never closed (INFERRED leak; no close() in repo). Also used by ChatOpenAI (orchestrator.py L228) and both CBORG clients. When pinning is active, the custom httpx.Client replaces the openai SDK's default client; INFERRED: openai's DefaultHttpxClient timeout/limits defaults are then not applied at the transport level, though the SDK still passes per-request timeout. openai_http_kwargs itself has no direct unit test (tests target _local_address).

There is NO per-request override: ChatRequest has no model/backend (api.py L124-145), ui_settings is trace-only (L3552). Changing backend via PUT without a model resets model to steps (3)-(5) (L2736-2739). _active_model() re-resolves on every LLM call (L2593-2595) but runtime.model is always set, so (1)/(2) win. Backend: PUT /settings backend (^(cborg|ollama)$, L412) > CLI --backend (cli.py L85, default 'cborg') coerced to cborg unless in {cborg, ollama} (api.py L2502); KG_RAG_BACKEND env is NOT consulted for the main-app runtime backend. items.description: Sufficiency-judge system prompt. Imported by retrieval_agent.py L44-48 (it is NOT defined in retrieval_agent.py). Defines three question classes and their bars: A) conceptual/overview/teaching/compare/how-to/example-code -> SUFFICIENT when retrieved nodes are on-topic; synthesize; disclose graph gaps first then elaborate; B) specific numeric/measurement claims (photon energy, eV, q-range, temperature, counts, a paper's measured value) -> SUFFICIENT only when slot/snippet/property is present, never invent numbers; C) hardware layout / beam path at ALS 11.0.1.2 -> ordered path from ops KG (graph_id bl1101) along beam_path_next/upstream_of/feeds/connected_to; never CyRSoXS/NRSS/YBCO/cuprate. Hard rules 1-6: prefer context for measurement facts, conceptual intents MAY use history + high-level domain knowledge marked 'not a KG measurement fact'; never invent authors/years/DOIs/journals/numbers/papers; empty or off-topic context -> sufficient=false; missing photon_energy is not insufficient for conceptual; cite [KG: graph_id: NodeName] copied from 'Allowed citations', [PDF: filename p.N], [OPS: file §heading], [MP: mp-id formula]; never fuse PDF with OPS/MP; no [1] numeric citations or References list; CodeSnippet reproduction must be followed by krag.CODE_SNIPPET_DISCLAIMER. Output: a SINGLE JSON object {sufficient, answer, missing_topics}.
items.notes: text_sha256 is sha256 of the RUNTIME string: AST-resolved concatenation with the CODE_SNIPPET_DISCLAIMER literal substituted (not a single ast.Constant). Tests only assert substrings; nothing freezes the full text. Changing CODE_SNIPPET_DISCLAIMER silently changes JUDGE_SYSTEM.

items.description: Leeway (second-pass) system prompt for non-layout questions: first say what the graph lacks, then elaborate from nodes, publication titles, related techniques (NRSS, CyRSoXS, Nika, P-RSoXS), conversation and high-level domain knowledge; mark domain-knowledge sentences 'not a KG measurement fact'; never invent numbers or papers/authors/DOIs; layout questions -> ops-only ordered path; return plain text, not JSON.
items.notes: Contains no citation-format instruction at all (unlike JUDGE_SYSTEM).

items.description: Leeway system prompt for hardware-layout questions: ordered path along directed edges source -> EPU/optics -> M103 -> exit slits -> ... -> sample -> detector; cite [KG: bl1101: NodeName] copied exactly; if topology thin say so then list ops hardware nodes; do not mention CyRSoXS, NRSS, Nika, P-RSoXS, YBCO, cuprate or the science KG; no invented numbers; plain text.

Deterministic question-class routers. _is_numeric_claim (L174-176) = _NUMERIC_CLAIM_RE.search. _is_ops_layout_question (L179-181) = _OPS_LAYOUT_RE.search. _is_conceptual_question (L184-193): empty -> False; numeric claim -> False (numeric wins); ops-layout -> True; else _CONCEPTUAL_QUESTION_RE. The word 'beamline' is deliberately not numeric (comment L64-65).
items.notes: Pattern hashes are of the re.compile first-arg literal (implicit concatenation folded by the parser). text_sha256 null because three patterns are involved; see contract.

items.description: Returns LAYOUT_LEEWAY_SYSTEM if _is_ops_layout_question(question) else LEEWAY_SYSTEM.

Formats history for judge AND leeway prompts: last 8 messages (history[-8:]); role defaults to 'user'; messages with empty content skipped; each content truncated to 1200 chars; output 'Conversation so far:
' + 'role: content' lines + '

', or '' when empty.
items.notes: No direct unit test. Unlike api._history_payload, roles are NOT filtered here (any role string passes through, incl. 'system' if a caller supplied it). Assistant turns (prior answers) are included verbatim.
text_sha256 = sha256(ast.unparse(JoinedStr at L244-248)). Retrieved context is placed raw after a plain-text header; no delimiters.

items.description: JSON leeway on judge output: empty raw -> {sufficient False, answer None, missing_topics []}. Finds all balanced {...} objects (regex supports nesting depth up to 3), tries them longest-first with json.loads, first dict containing key 'sufficient' wins: answer defaulted to None; missing_topics coerced (str -> [str], non-list -> [], stripped non-empty); sufficient coerced via _coerce_bool (L122-128: bool as-is; strings 'true'/'yes'/'1' -> True, other strings False; else bool()); sufficient with blank answer forced False. No match -> {sufficient False, answer None, missing_topics [], raw}.
items.notes: A JSON object nested deeper than 3 levels is not matched as a whole; inner objects could be tried instead (inferred from regex). Non-JSON prose answers are discarded -> insufficient.

items.description: Node counts as direct evidence if raw node has source_papers/publications/context_snippets/code_snippet, OR non-empty description (raw or payload), OR category/type/raw_category containing any of _TECHNIQUE_CATEGORY_HINTS (L72-91: measurement, technique, method, instrument, scattering, publication, paper, codesnippet, beamline, beamlinestage, endstation, motor, detector, processvariable, esaf, proposal, sample, blueskyrun), OR any out-edge with has_evidence/evidence/source_papers. Graph degree alone is not enough.
items.notes: Substring match on category: e.g. 'sample' matches 'SampleClass'; any described node passes.

items.description: no_evidence = (no selected hits AND chunk_count==0 AND no MP context) OR (direct_evidence_count==0 AND chunk_count==0 AND not conceptual AND no MP context). If true: no context build, no LLM call; returns status 'success', sufficient False, answer None, missing_topics [question], no_evidence True, direct_evidence_count 0 (forced 0 even if computed otherwise).

contract.conceptual_bypass: conceptual questions with >=1 selected hit always reach the judge

items.notes: MP context alone suppresses no_evidence even with zero KG hits.

items.description: If _build_merged_context raises: if source_context (hybrid+MP) non-empty, it becomes ctx and flow continues to the judge; otherwise returns status 'context_error', sufficient False, missing_topics [question], error=str(exc).
items.notes: Untested. 'context_error' ends with '_error' so api treats it as retrieval_error (api.py L5150).

items.description: make_chat_client(backend, model) + krag.call_llm(cli, Conversation(JUDGE_SYSTEM).build(prompt), 'KG-RAG-judge') -> messages [system JUDGE_SYSTEM, user judge prompt]. Any exception (incl. client construction, timeout) -> status 'judge_error', sufficient False, missing [question], error str.

contract.timeout: krag.LLM_TIMEOUT (env KG_RAG_LLM_TIMEOUT, default 120) +5s asyncio.wait_for (kg_rag_api.py L116, L1602)

items.description: sufficient = parsed verdict; if insufficient and no missing_topics -> [question]; answer kept only if sufficient. Leeway second pass runs iff NOT sufficient AND (selected hits OR chunk_count>0) AND NOT numeric claim. Non-empty leeway text -> sufficient=True, answer=leeway text.

contract.numeric_claims: never get leeway at this layer; remain sufficient=False
contract.mp_only: MP-only context (no hits, no chunks) does not trigger leeway

items.notes: RISK: result dict carries no 'leeway' key, so downstream api._json_graph_nodes_address_question (api.py L1978 'genuine = sufficient and not verdict.get("leeway")') treats a leeway answer as a genuine judge-sufficient answer. Leeway is NOT restricted to conceptual questions: any non-numeric question with hits qualifies (including 'other' class).

items.description:
Second-pass LLM call, label 'KG-RAG-leeway', system leeway_system_for(question). User prompt = history block + 'Question:
..

Graph gaps to disclose:
{missing}

Retrieved Context:
{ctx or (empty)}

Write the answer now.' Uses the same cli as the judge. Exception -> None (stays insufficient, note_error). Returns stripped text or None; no JSON parse, no citation validation.
items.notes: Default missing_text (L1459-1461) appears unreachable from query() because missing is always non-empty there (L1360-1361) — inferred.

items.description: Final result: status 'success', question, sufficient, answer (None unless sufficient), missing_topics, selected (hit ids), selected_hits (ScoredHit.as_dict), no_evidence False, direct_evidence_count, plus _source_meta (graph_source_requested/used, graph_ids, kg_query_hops, kg_query_max_nodes, live_tiled, kg_intent, materials_project) and hybrid_meta {hybrid_rag{intent,chunk_count,literature_available,ops_available}, materials_project}.
items.notes: 'status' is 'success' for both sufficient and insufficient verdicts; sufficiency is carried only by the boolean.

items.description: Layout questions: hops = max(kg_query_hops, LAYOUT_KG_QUERY_HOPS=16) (L92, L957); only bl1101* (ops) graphs if any loaded, else all non-Tiled; plus documented beam-path stages (_beam_path_nodeinfos L311-372, score 2.0+(50-index)/50); plus _substring_device_fallback (L743-793: node names >=4 chars appearing verbatim in question, score 1.5, limit 10); if still no hits, retry on science graphs. Non-layout: _classify_query_intent then _intent_routed_retrieve. Always merge_hits(raw, limit=max_nodes). Tiled graph excluded from fan-out.
items.notes: self._last_intent is only updated on the non-layout branch (L972), so for layout questions _build_kg_context ordering uses the previous turn's intent (inferred staleness).

items.description: _classify_query_intent (L157-171): first match of _TILED_INTENT_RE -> 'tiled', _OPS_INTENT_RE -> 'ops', _LITERATURE_INTENT_RE -> 'literature', else 'general'. _intent_routed_retrieve (L868-939): general or <=1 graph -> equal _parallel_retrieve; ops/tiled -> bl1101* graphs primary; literature -> non-ops primary; primary max=int(max_nodes*0.6), each secondary max=int(max_nodes*0.4/len(secondary)) (min 1). Literature: if science-graph hits < 0.3*max_nodes, add _rsoxs_popular_nodes (L796-866: nodes with >=2 papers, score 0.3+count/100).
items.notes: _rsoxs_popular_nodes untested. 'tiled' intent words include generic 'samples?', 'measurements?', 'run' so many science questions route ops-primary (inferred from regex).

items.description: Despite the name, iterates graphs sequentially (docstring L686-700: avoids nested thread pools/OOM). Per graph: krag.retrieve_nodes(q, kg, hops, max_nodes) with TypeError fallback to old signature (_call_retrieve_nodes L303-308); AttributeError/TypeError re-raised, other exceptions -> [] for that graph.

Per-graph context sections. Order: literature intent -> science graphs first; ops/tiled -> bl1101* first; general -> score insertion order. Each section header: '### Knowledge graph `{gid}` ({label}). Cite nodes from this graph as [KG: {gid}: <name>].' followed by 'Allowed citations (copy these tokens exactly):' and one '- [KG: {gid}: {name}]' line per hit. Body = kg.build_context(infos, include_structured=krag.STRUCT_CTX, char_budget=remaining, hint_terms=tokenize(q), include_pdf_snippets=False). Shared budget starts at krag.CTX_SOFT_LIMIT and is reduced by len(header+ctx); loop stops when remaining<=0.
items.notes: No test asserts the 'Allowed citations' block or token format. Allowed-citation header text is NOT counted against the char_budget passed into build_context, and build_context checks budget after appending a section, so total context can exceed CTX_SOFT_LIMIT. Allowed list includes every hit even if its section was cut by budget.

items.description: Merged ctx = '\n\n'.join of non-blank [KG context, source_context]; source_context = hybrid ContextBuilder output + MP context.

Default self._source_rag = hybrid_rag_enabled() (pipeline.py L55-60: env F2W_SOURCE_RAG, else HYBRID_RAG_ENABLED, default '0' -> off) unless constructor arg given (L409); set_source_rag (L488-490); per-call query(source_rag=...) overrides (L1200). Off -> empty pack, chunk_count 0. On -> HybridSourceRAG.pack(include_literature=not layout, include_ops=True, layout, numeric, kg_work_ids from source_papers basenames + 'doi:<doi>', kg_entity_ids); any exception -> empty pack + note_error.

Source-RAG packing (6000 chars default, L9). Budget shares by intent: layout lit 15%/ops 85%; why_how 70/30; else 55/45. KG index first (max 12 items, '[KG:{gid}: {name}] (category) score=x'), then 'Literature source evidence' with [PDF: name p.N], then 'Beamline ops-doc evidence (bl1101)' with [OPS: file §heading], then Tiled run metadata (max 800 chars) with [TILED: id]. Sections truncate the last block if >=80 chars remain.
items.notes: KG-index tokens here use '[KG:{gid}: name]' (NO space after 'KG:'), differing from retrieval_agent's '[KG: {gid}: name]'; both can appear in the same merged context.

items.description: lookup_materials_project(question) ALWAYS runs (independent of source_rag). materials_project.py L90-130: triggers only if formulas/mp-ids are extracted; requires MP_API_KEY else skipped='no_api_key'; up to 3 queries, max 3 unique records. format_mp_context (L156-191) emits '### Materials Project', 'Allowed citations (copy these tokens exactly):', '[MP: mp-id formula]' tokens and numeric properties (band_gap_eV, energy_above_hull_eV, formation_energy_per_atom_eV, density_g_cm3, spacegroup, url). MP context is appended to source_context and counts as evidence (has_mp).
items.notes: MP supplies numeric properties, so a numeric claim can be judged sufficient from MP records; MP network call happens even with source RAG disabled.

items.description: live_tiled off -> meta status 'disabled', no change. On but not is_experiment_identity_question -> status 'skipped'. Else lookup_experiment_identity; if graph has nodes it is added as graph_id 'tiled' (also persisted into self._graphs); hits merged with KG hits via merge_hits(limit=kg_query_max_nodes). Tiled context header (tiled_graph.py L386-390) instructs '[KG:tiled: ESAF 2026-00043]' citations.
items.notes: The Tiled graph written into self._graphs persists for later queries until reload (inferred from L628-631; _fanout_hits excludes it from fan-out but _active_graphs returns it).

items.description: Hops clamped 1..20 (MAX_KG_QUERY_HOPS=20, default 20); max_nodes clamped 10..1000 (default 1000). RetrievalAgent stores clamped values (retrieval_agent.py L404-405, L481-486). Other kg_rag_api limits: CONTEXT_CHAR_BUDGET 16000 (env KG_RAG_CTX_CHARS), CTX_SOFT_LIMIT 0.75x, PDF_SNIPPET_LEN 1000, CTX_VOLUME_TRIPLES 150, STRUCT_CTX on (kg_rag_api.py L141-165), LLM_TIMEOUT 120 (L116).
items.notes: Defaults are maxima: every query uses 20 hops / 1000 nodes unless settings lower them.

items.description: Renders 'Structured_KG_Facts:' triples (<=150) among rendered nodes, then per node '## {name} ({category})', Combined_Score, Description, Formula, Source_Papers, Publications / scalar metadata (suppressed when >1 source paper), CodeSnippet fields + fenced code (snippet nodes without code are skipped), optional raw PDF snippet tagged '[PDF {pdf}]' (no colon), Relations to rendered nodes. Stops after the node that crosses char_budget. ANSI stripped.
items.notes: Raw PDF tag '[PDF file.pdf]' differs from cite syntax '[PDF: file.pdf]'; build_rag_prompt docstring tells the model to convert. Retrieval agent disables PDF snippets.

items.description: System prompt for the legacy CLI answer() and the OpenWebUI proxy (create_fastapi_app). Strict: 'Use ONLY the Retrieved Context for scientific claims. Never add outside or domain knowledge. If evidence is missing, state the gap'; cite [KG: NodeName] / [PDF: file.pdf]; publication metadata forbidden unless verbatim in context; reproduce CodeSnippet code completely + CODE_SNIPPET_DISCLAIMER.
items.notes: Opposite policy to JUDGE_SYSTEM/LEEWAY_SYSTEM (which allow labeled domain knowledge). Not used by the F2W agent path. resolved_sha256 substitutes CODE_SNIPPET_DISCLAIMER into the f-string.

items.description: Non-RAG baseline system prompt (answer() only when SHOW_BASELINE, env KG_RAG_SHOW_BASELINE default 0).
Verbatim disclaimer the model must append after reproduced CodeSnippet code; embedded in JUDGE_SYSTEM, RAG_SYSTEM and build_rag_prompt.
items.notes: Never validated server-side; presence in answers is model-dependent.

items.description: Legacy CLI QA: retrieve_nodes(q, kg) (module defaults), build_context(STRUCT_CTX, CTX_SOFT_LIMIT, PDF snippets ON), optional baseline call, RAG call label 'KG-RAG' with rag_c (RAG_SYSTEM); prints result; rag_c.add() appends every turn (unbounded multi-turn history). No sufficiency judge, no status, returns None. Gap logging: all infos evidence_ct==0 -> MissingNode 'no evidence in KG'; each '[Domain Knowledge]...' line in the answer -> 'llm_fallback'.
items.notes: No direct test of answer(). The sibling OpenWebUI proxy path create_fastapi_app._answer_messages (L219-243) is stateless (uses only messages[-1], never rag_c.add) and is covered by tests/test_fastapi_endpoints.py::TestApiChat::test_returns_assistant_response, ::TestGapTracking::test_logs_missing_node_on_zero_evidence, ::TestGapTracking::test_logs_domain_knowledge_fallback. '[Domain Knowledge]' detection is vestigial given RAG_SYSTEM forbids domain knowledge.

items.description: Conversation(system).build(user) -> [{system}, ...history..., {user}] without mutating state. call_llm: asyncio.wait_for(cli.chat(messages), LLM_TIMEOUT+5); TimeoutError -> RuntimeError('<label> call exceeded ...'); every call (success/failure) recorded via trace.record_llm_call.

12 actions: direct_response, retrieve_kg, query_extracted_paper, report_extraction, search_candidates, consult_debate, request_download_approval, download_selected, request_extraction_approval, extract_selected, clarify, stop_insufficient; each bound to one agent. Fresh-turn classes: mundane_conversation, irrelevant_non_scientific, scientific_or_uncertain, ops_layout. DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS=12.

Deterministic precedence: steps>=max_steps -> stop_insufficient; pending download/extraction -> download_selected/extract_selected only with matching one-use approval token, else request_*_approval; route_hint retrieve_kg in phase paper_extracted -> retrieve_kg; extracted-terms follow-up or hint -> report_extraction; active-paper reference or hint -> query_extracted_paper; terminal phases (stop_insufficient, retrieval_error, extraction_error, orchestration_stopped) -> stop_insufficient; retrieval_insufficient -> search_candidates; post_extraction_insufficient -> stop_insufficient; candidates_found -> consult_debate; candidate_selected -> request_download_approval; paper_downloaded -> request_extraction_approval; paper_extracted -> retrieve_kg; hint direct_response -> direct_response; greeting regex fullmatch -> direct_response; ops layout -> retrieve_kg(ops_layout); else retrieve_kg(scientific_or_uncertain).

items.description: Fresh-turn classifier prompt (term_extractor client, temperature 0.0, timeout 60, label 'orchestrator-classify'). Model only classifies, never selects actions; memory 'is never scientific evidence'; hard rules: never refuse as out of scope, uncertain -> scientific_or_uncertain, meta follow-ups ('be more general', 'try again') -> scientific_or_uncertain. STATE exposes phase, current_topic, has_active_extracted_paper, active_paper_title. Output parsed with greedy first-{...}-last-} regex + json.loads.

items.description: Rejects (None) unless: action in ACTIONS; proposed agent equals bound agent; agent available; with pending, action must equal the single required action (approval-token match); action allowed in phase_actions[phase] (L405-418) when phase listed; download_selected needs matching download approval + in-range, not-unavailable candidate_index; extract_selected needs matching approval + active_paper.status=='downloaded'; query_extracted_paper/report_extraction need active_paper.status=='extracted' and matching/None paper_id. Returns normalized _decision.
items.notes: Phases absent from phase_actions (e.g. 'direct_responded', 'stop_insufficient', 'retrieval_error') impose no phase restriction.

items.description: decide: compute fallback; if fallback is direct_response/query_extracted_paper/report_extraction and validates -> return it (no LLM). If pending, phase!='idle', or route_hint -> validated fallback else stop_insufficient. Otherwise LLM classify (exception -> {}); ops-layout regex overrides classification to ops_layout; _fresh_turn_decision maps mundane_conversation -> direct_response, other valid classes -> retrieve_kg, unknown -> None; validate proposal, else validated fallback, else stop_insufficient.
items.notes: irrelevant_non_scientific still retrieves the KG (no topic refusal).

items.description: Heuristic: probe sufficient -> answer_from_kg; no candidates -> stop_insufficient; best candidate score (score or _score) < MIN_FALLBACK_SCORE=0.12 -> stop_insufficient; else download_selected [best_idx]. It ranks OpenAlex title/abstract candidates by their pre-computed score only.

items.description: Prompt: controller with internal roles (Retrieval advocate, Literature scout, Critic), no transcript; allowed actions answer_from_kg (only if probe sufficient), refine_search, download_selected (<=1), stop_insufficient; JSON keys hypothesis, objections, selected_action, reason, candidate_indices, refined_query. Inputs: ROUND, QUESTION, RETRIEVAL_PROBE json[:4000], CANDIDATES (first 6, abstract[:1400]). Post-validation: unknown action -> _fallback_decide; answer_from_kg w/o sufficient -> stop_insufficient; indices filtered to range; download_selected w/o indices -> [0]; selected max score <0.12 -> stop_insufficient. decide() exception -> _fallback_decide. Output dict: hypothesis, objections, selected_action, reason, candidate_titles (selected or first 3), candidate_indices, refined_query.

Claims = non-heading, non-label lines (bullets/numbering stripped) split into sentences on [.!?]+space not followed by '[PDF:'; every claim with a letter must contain a page citation.
items.notes: Validated against ALL eligible pages, not the <=8 pages actually supplied in full mode, so a citation to an eligible-but-unsent page passes. Only PDF citations are validated anywhere server-side.

items.description: Reads eligible pages with PyMuPDF; ranks non-empty pages by query-token overlap then length; full mode sends top MAX_LLM_PAGES=8, targeted mode sends ALL eligible pages; each page text[:MAX_PAGE_CHARS=7000] under '--- {file} PAGE {n} ---'. Prompt: ONLY supplied pages; JSON keys status, sufficient, answer, used_pages, missing_topics; every factual sentence/bullet cited exactly like [PDF: {file} p.N]; if unanswerable, sufficient=false with explicit insufficiency statement; do not propose downloading/searching.

Parses JSON (greedy regex). sufficient = bool(result['sufficient']); used_pages filtered to supplied pages. If sufficient and citation errors -> ONE repair prompt (VALIDATION_ERRORS, CANDIDATE_ANSWER, pages); repaired accepted only if sufficient and zero errors, else answer replaced by fixed failure text, sufficient False. Outcomes: 'paper_llm_error' (chat exception), 'insufficient' (answer or 'The eligible extracted pages do not answer this question.'), 'success'.
items.notes: RISK: bool() not _coerce_bool -> a JSON string "false" is truthy; the model's 'status' field is ignored; insufficient answers are model text passed through unvalidated.

items.description: Deterministic (no LLM) page-cited term summary. Eligible pages: top-level selected_pages else last partial; if state 'full' and none, union of the terms' pages. Term pages = context_snippet pages for this file ∩ eligible, else term.pages ∩ eligible. Query-scoped ranking (100 node-name match + 8/2/1 token overlaps), else round-robin by first page. Lines '- **term** (category): definition [PDF: {file} p.{page}]'. Statuses: manifest_error, insufficient, success (+term_count, relevant_term_count, displayed_term_count, relevance_mode matched|query_targeted_pages|all_terms). Default max_terms 16; post-extraction uses 6 (api.py L6359).
items.notes: Eligibility rules differ from _eligible_pages: full.selected_pages is ignored and a full extraction is bounded by term pages, not all pages.

items.description: Per round: _query_retrieval -> exception or status '*_error' -> 'retrieval_error'. json_needs_ingest = json source and _json_graph_should_search_candidates. sufficient and not needs_ingest -> 'answered' (verdict answer). JSON and not needs_ingest -> canned refusal 'insufficient_json_graph' if _json_graph_should_use_canned_refusal else JSON leeway answer -> 'answered' with verdict copy {sufficient True, leeway True}. Otherwise (splash, or JSON needing ingest): recently-declined -> 'stop_insufficient'; orchestrator must allow search_candidates (else stop_insufficient); candidate search (missing -> agent_unavailable, exception -> candidate_search_error, none -> stop_insufficient); orchestrator must allow consult_debate; debate (missing -> agent_unavailable, exception -> debate_error); refine_search once; answer_from_kg only if verdict sufficient and not needs_ingest -> 'answered'; else pending download -> 'awaiting_download_decision' with CANDIDATE_PAPERS_INTRO or _UNRANKED_INTRO. Loop end -> 'max_rounds'.

items.description: nodes_address_question: False if no_evidence/no selected or no token overlap between significant question tokens and selected ids/names; genuine (sufficient and no 'leeway' key) -> True unless answer admits a missing asked concept (_LACKS_CONCEPT_RE); else False if comparative/optimization, or missing topics not all slot gaps (_JSON_GRAPH_SLOT_GAP_RE or numeric), or answer admits missing concept; else conceptual or ops-layout. should_search_candidates = explicit paper ingest request (_direct_download_request or _FIND_PAPER_RE) or not nodes_address_question. canned refusal = no_evidence/no selected, else not conceptual and numeric.

Per round: retrieval_started; _query_retrieval; retrieval_result; graph_update if selected; *_error verdict -> retrieval_error; sufficient and not json_needs_ingest -> answered; JSON non-ingest -> insufficient_json_graph (canned refusal) or leeway 'answered'; else phase retrieval_insufficient, JSON-mode decline guard -> stop_insufficient; up to 2 preflights: orchestrator must say search_candidates, candidate_search_started, DownloadAgent.search_candidates (cfg.candidate_pool), none -> stop_insufficient; orchestrator must say consult_debate; candidate_search_result; debate_started; EvidenceDebateAgent.decide; debate_result; refine_search on preflight 1 -> action_selected + retry. Then action_selected; answer_from_kg+sufficient -> answered; else build download pending (5450-5470) with candidate_list = [best,*alternatives] (best+3 when debate chose download_selected, else candidates[:4] with recommended_candidate_index None), phase awaiting_download_approval, orchestrator decision, awaiting_download_decision event, return status awaiting_download_decision with pending payload.

items.description: Any /chat message while a pending exists is consumed as a reply to it. Extraction pending (4120-4136): regex \b(yes|approve|extract|run extraction|go ahead|continue)\b -> act yes; else \b(no|decline|skip|cancel|do not|don't)\b -> act no; else orchestrator decision and re-prompt status awaiting_extraction_decision. Download pending (5877-5906): heuristic (5745-5818) then LLM fallback (5820-5875, label 'pending-download-intent', 60s). Heuristic: decline words (don't|do not|no download|none|neither|decline|cancel|skip all|skip download) unless '...but...download' -> decline; exact yes/approve/approved/go ahead/continue -> recommended non-failed index or clarify if none; download verb + another|next|different -> first non-failed; download verb + 'candidate|paper|option N' -> N-1; ordinals first..fourth/'recommended'; 'arxiv' -> first arXiv candidate; title token overlap >= 0.5; single candidate + download verb -> 0. LLM result action in download|decline|clarify|new_question; out-of-range download -> clarify. decline -> _act_locked('no'); download -> _act_locked('yes', candidate_index); clarify/new_question -> re-prompt awaiting_download_decision.

contract.selection_index_rules: heuristic first, then LLM; recommended index = pending.recommended_candidate_index if key present (None for unranked lists), else first non-failed index (5726-5743)

items.notes: Risky: an LLM interpretation of free text can approve a download; 'new_question' is treated like clarify, so a user cannot ask a new question while a download pending exists until they decline, start a new chat (new session id), or reset. Heuristic 'yes' is unanchored for extraction (e.g. 'yes but don't' -> yes because yes regex is tested first). Decline regex matches 'none' anywhere.

items.description: act*: open trace with message=decision and parent_turn_id; note_request(message=decision, effective_question=decision); under self.lock _activate_session then _act_locked. _act_locked: _normalize_pending_state; none -> no_pending_action; kind mismatch -> ValueError; decision 'no' -> _set_pending(None, phase='stopped_by_user'), approved_action=None, download decline recorded in declined_download_topics, status stopped_by_user (publications_override=[] only for extraction decline), memory finalized. Download yes: candidate_index required, in range of candidate_list, not in workflow.unavailable_candidate_indices -> else ValueError; write approved_action{kind,approval_token,candidate_index}; orchestrator must return download_selected else ValueError('Download approval did not match the pending action'); approved_action cleared, phase downloading, _resume_download. Extraction yes: approved_action{kind:'extraction',approval_token}; orchestrator must return extract_selected else ValueError; phase extracting; _resume_extraction.

contract.consumes_pending: on no; on download/extraction completion paths (see ST-20/21)
errors: Pending action is X, not Y
Download actions require decision=yes with a candidate_index
candidate_index is required to download a paper
Download approval did not match the pending action
Extraction approval did not match the pending action

items.notes: act does NOT reset workflow.orchestration_steps (only ask does at 3665/3681/3812/3828); see ST-26.

items.description: _set_pending writes pending (and optional phase) to workflow (persisted). _normalize_pending_state (3947-3981) setdefault approval_token=uuid4 hex, phase=f'awaiting_{kind}_approval', mirrors candidate_list into workflow.candidates for download, or synthesizes active_paper{status:'downloaded'} from downloaded[0] for extraction if missing. _remember_pending_meta (4214-4228) setdefaults original_question, effective_question, graph_source, json_graph_path on the pending and persists.
items.notes: Pending carries full verdict and candidate dicts (abstracts etc.) to disk in workflow_state.json.

items.description: Emits download_started; DownloadAgent.download_selected(question, missing_topics, target_dir=coord.pdf_dir, candidates=[best], max_papers=1, validate_downloads=False, refresh_urls=True). Missing method -> clear pending, agent_unavailable. Exception -> clear pending, phase stop_insufficient, status download_error. Emits download_result. count==0 -> keep download pending with failed_candidate_indices (+selected index), workflow.unavailable_candidate_indices, status awaiting_download_decision with failure message. Success -> active_paper{status:'downloaded'}, new extraction pending with fresh approval_token, phase awaiting_extraction_approval, orchestrator decision, awaiting_extraction_decision event, status awaiting_extraction_decision (answer '').
items.notes: download_error ends with '_error' -> SSE 'error' event, so the UI shows 'Agent run failed: <answer>' rather than a normal message.

items.description: Runs _extract_rebuild_reload on pending.downloaded; failure -> clear pending (phase=failure.status), finalize memory, return failure. Success -> active_paper.status='extracted', clear pending (phase paper_extracted), record extraction summary; orchestrator with route_hint retrieve_kg must say retrieve_kg else orchestration_stopped. Emits retrieval_started ('re-checking'), re-queries, builds term report and post-extraction answer, emits retrieval_result and graph_update (if display ids). Status retrieval_error / answered / insufficient_evidence (the latter appends DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE_FALLBACK_DISCLAIMER + LLM domain answer, label 'domain-knowledge-fallback'). Approved candidate publication merged into publications.
items.notes: [INFERRED] After extraction, retrieval is reloaded with coord.session_kg only (5692), but the next fresh /chat turn reloads the JSON selection (5076-5081), so in JSON mode newly extracted terms are only visible to the immediate re-check unless kg.json is among the selected paths. Verify before migration.

items.description: Stage unprocessed approved PDFs (none -> no_unprocessed_pdfs). extraction_started {round,pdfs,mode,max_pages}; targeted -> extractor.extract_targeted(round_dir, session_terms, question, missing, targeted_max_pages) else extractor.extract; error -> extraction_error. extraction_result {round,mode,term_count,processed_files,processed_pages_total,processed_pages_with_terms}; manifests updated. kg_rebuild_started; kg_update.rebuild_kg (synchronous call on the event loop); kg_rebuild_result {round,node_count,edge_count}. If cfg.kg_mode=='splash': splash_reimport_started; kg_update.splash_reimport(session_kg, splash_repo, allow_wipe=cfg.allow_splash_wipe) (synchronous subprocess, timeout 900s at kg_update.py 193); splash_reimport_result {round,status}. reload_started; retrieval.reload_kg(session_kg); reload_result {round,node_count,status}. Returns None on success.
items.notes: rebuild_kg and splash_reimport are called synchronously inside an async function, blocking the event loop (all other requests, including SSE flushing of other streams) for their duration [INFERRED from call shape]. Splash branch keys on cfg.kg_mode, not runtime.graph_source.

items.description: _response builds ChatResponse: node_ids = query-graph node ids or verdict.selected; publications = override or publications_for_selected_nodes(graph_path, selected_ids); graph = _query_graph_payload; orchestration = _last_orchestration; turn_id = current_turn_id(). _direct_response (4138-4165) sets phase direct_responded and returns status direct_response, confidence 1.0, full graph_payload_from_file(graph_path) (whole graph, not a subset), rounds=[{routing:{requires_agents:false,reason}}].

items.description: Adds turn_id (setdefault) to payload, records note_progress in trace even when emit is None, then awaits emit(event, message, payload). In the stream routes the final SSE data = {phase, message, turn_id, **payload}.
items.notes: Trace 'progress' records all phases for non-streaming /chat too.

items.description: Deterministic gate. _safe_fallback: steps >= max_steps -> stop_insufficient (181-182); pending download -> download_selected only if approved_action.kind==pending.kind and approval_token matches, else request_download_approval; pending extraction -> extract_selected only on token match, else request_extraction_approval (186-213); then phase-driven transitions (244-267). validate (368-465): with a pending, only the required action is accepted; per-phase allow-lists (405-418); download_selected requires token match and candidate_index within state.candidates and not unavailable (421-434); extract_selected requires token match and active_paper.status=='downloaded' (435-443). decide (467-516): LLM classification (label 'orchestrator-classify', 60s, 299-352) only when no pending, phase=='idle' and no route_hint; LLM output can only map to direct_response or retrieve_kg; failures fall back to safe deterministic decision.

contract.approval_token_is_one_use: approved_action is cleared right after match (api.py 6105, 6116)

items.notes: The LLM never proposes download/extract; approvals are entirely state/token driven.

items.description: Each _orchestrator_decision increments workflow.orchestration_steps (4005, 4015-4018). ask resets it to 0 (3665, 3681, 3812, 3828) but act/act_with_progress and _handle_pending_message (which runs before the reset at 3661/3808) do not. max_steps = cfg.max_orchestration_steps default 12 (api.py 2626, coordinator.py 93).
items.notes: [INFERRED] A full flow (ask: classify + search + debate + post-pending = 4, +2 per refine_search; download approval: +2; extraction approval: +2) stays under 12, but repeated failed-download retries, re-prompts, or refine loops accumulate within one pending lifecycle; on exhaustion the approval check returns stop_insufficient and _act_locked raises ValueError ('approval did not match') -> 400 / SSE stream_error. Not covered end-to-end.

items.description: Declining a download stores effective/original question in workflow.declined_download_topics (case-insensitive dedupe, last 5 kept). In _ask_locked (5228-5246), JSON mode only and not an explicit download request: if >=50% of the shorter side's 4+-char tokens overlap a declined topic, return stop_insufficient without searching.
items.notes: Untested. Cleared only by session reset/delete (workflow.clear).

items.description: _finalize_memory records the turn (user message, effective question, answer, status, sufficient, node_ids, publications, rounds) then, if summary >= 2400 chars, runs memory.compress in a thread executor using self._labeled_completion(prompt, timeout=60, label='session-memory-compress') i.e. the same runtime backend/model as chat (CBORG or Ollama via term_extractor.clients.make_chat_client, 4615-4630). Exceptions noted to trace and swallowed.

items.notes: Untested.

items.description: Topic-scoped context (summary clip 1000, 5 open questions, up to 16 entities, last 3 KG growth events, last 4 current-topic turns clip 180), clipped to 2600 chars. Injected into prompts: legacy router (api.py 4511), direct response (4556), rewrite (4646), pending-download intent (5847). Not injected into retrieval/grounded answers (docstring 3-6).

Route 6657-6660 accepts optional body {session_id}; invalid id -> 422. Delete: key validated (ValueError -> 400 at route 6662-6668); '__legacy__' cannot be deleted; under lock, if active switches to legacy, drops in-memory context, rmtree <workdir>/chat_sessions/<key>; returns {status:'deleted', session_id}.

items.description: JSON control-plane state, version 1: current_query, current_topic, phase, last_route, candidates, unavailable_candidate_indices, active_paper, approved_action, extraction, post_extraction_sufficient, pending, round_no, orchestration_steps, declined_download_topics, updated_at. save(): tempfile in same dir + fsync + os.replace (atomic). update(**values) merges and saves on every call. clear() resets and saves. pending property returns a deepcopy. Corrupt/non-dict file -> defaults; non-list fields coerced.

Record fields: schema_version, turn_id, session_id, parent_turn_id, started_at, finished_at, env{git_sha,backend,models{chat,orchestrator,judge,leeway},settings(F2W_*/KG_RAG_* env, redacted),graphs[{path,sha256}]}, request{message,effective_question,history,graph_source,json_graph_paths,source_rag,use_live_tiled,ui_settings}, orchestration{raw_classifier_output,classification,decision (FIRST decision only, 421-426),prechecks}, progress[{name,message,data,offset_ms}], retrieval{...}, llm_calls[{label,model,messages,system_prompt_sha256,response,latency_ms,timeout,error}], response{answer,citations{kg,pdf,ops},publications,pending,status,sufficient,confidence,elapsed_seconds}, errors[]. finish() redacts secrets and writes once; never raises.

items.description: Trigger: question contains mp-<digits> ids or formula-like tokens (regex + pymatgen Composition parse, stop tokens excluded); bare digit-less single-element tokens are dropped unless a property cue (band gap, space group, density, materials project, stable...) or a >=2-element token is present. Up to 3 queries, limit 3 records total, dedup by material_id; per-query exceptions -> skipped 'search_error'. search_mp_summary uses mp_api.client.MPRester(key).materials.summary.search(fields=[material_id, formula_pretty, band_gap, energy_above_hull, formation_energy_per_atom, symmetry, density, is_stable, is_metal], num_chunks=1, chunk_size=limit, material_ids|formula). items.description: One asyncio.Lock per service guards _ask_body (3658), _ask_with_progress_body (3805), _act_body (5968), _act_with_progress_body (6024), apply_settings (2728), reset_session_context (4232), delete_session_context (4251). Held for the entire turn including LLM calls, OpenAlex search, PDF download, extraction, KG rebuild and splash import. run_api starts uvicorn with a single process (7034-7038).

contract.concurrency: all chat/action/settings/reset/delete requests across all sessions are serialized; second request waits (no timeout, no 409/429)

items.notes: Read endpoints (/health, /graph, /graph/node, /settings GET) are not locked and read whichever session is currently active (e.g. /health 6636-6640 reports pending_approval/workflow_phase of the last-activated session). For a queued SSE request, turn_started is enqueued before the service takes the lock (6839 vs 3805), so the client sees turn_started immediately and then silence until the lock frees [INFERRED].

items.description: All service LLM calls go through _labeled_completion(timeout=60): legacy-route 4518, direct-response 4563, domain-knowledge-fallback 4596, rewrite-question 4653, json-graph-leeway 4732, pending-download-intent 5855, session-memory-compress 4206; orchestrator-classify timeout=60 (orchestrator_agent.py 346-351). Splash graph load timeout=5 at init/settings (2581). Splash import subprocess timeout=900 (kg_update.py 193). git rev-parse timeout=2 (trace.py 198). No per-turn/overall request timeout, no SSE heartbeat, no MP timeout; retrieval/debate/download/extractor internal timeouts are outside this section.
items.notes: Timeouts are per call; a turn can chain many 60s calls while holding the global lock.

items.description: If active_paper.status=='extracted' and the turn references it (_paper_reference_followup) or asks for extracted terms (_extracted_terms_followup), orchestrator is consulted with route_hint and, if confirmed, PaperEvidenceAgent.query (paper LLM) or deterministic summarize_extracted_terms answers. Statuses: paper_answered / paper_insufficient / extraction_reported.
items.notes: These run before the workflow reset to idle, so they see the prior turn's phase.

sse.terminal: Exactly one 'complete' or 'error' frame then close. 'complete' carries the full ChatResponse JSON (turn_id ensured). 'error' carries the full ChatResponse JSON when response.status endswith '_error' (retrieval_error, candidate_search_error, debate_error, download_error, extraction_error, kg_rebuild_error, splash_error) (6878-6879 / 6969-6970). Non-error terminal statuses such as stop_insufficient, agent_unavailable, no_pending_action, stopped_by_user, insufficient_evidence go out as 'complete'.
sse.error_mid_stream: Any Exception raised by ask_with_progress/act_with_progress (ValueError for bad session id, kind mismatch, candidate_index problems, approval mismatch, JSON graph missing; or unexpected errors) is caught in run() and sent as event 'error' data {status:'stream_error', message:str(exc), turn_id} (6882-6890 / 6973-6981); HTTP status stays 200. The service has already called note_error and finish_turn. Progress frames already sent are not retracted; workflow state changes made before the exception persist (e.g. approved_action written at 6094-6100 before the orchestrator mismatch raise).
sse.cancellation: When the response generator is closed (client disconnect/abort; Starlette 1.3.1 per requirements/dev.txt 584) the generator's finally (6902-6906 / 6993-6997) cancels the run() task if still running and awaits it, suppressing CancelledError. [INFERRED] CancelledError is a BaseException so the service's 'except Exception' blocks do not catch it; finally blocks still run finish_turn (trace written without a response) and release self.lock via async with. Work already handed to run_in_executor threads (LLM calls, retrieval fan-out, MP lookup) keeps running to completion and its result is discarded. Synchronous blocking calls (kg_update.rebuild_kg, splash_reimport) cannot be interrupted. Workflow state may be left mid-transition (e.g. phase 'downloading'/'extracting' with pending still set); the next _act_locked/_normalize_pending_state resets phase to awaiting_<kind>_approval. No 'complete' or 'error' frame is sent on cancellation. Session memory is not recorded for a cancelled turn. Non-streaming /chat has no explicit disconnect handling [INFERRED: request runs to completion].

open_questions: Seam ids for api.py items: the brief only names B28/B29/B30/B33; api.py items are tagged B02 from the template example. Confirm the correct seam id(s) for routes/state/SSE.
